teaching_phrase: Before we play faster or learn more, we check if the body is available.
activity: Breath shoulders jaw hands open-string sound
step_down_if_stuck: One breath and one open string

teaching_phrase: A right-hand pattern is rhythm you can hold. It gives the left hand somewhere to live.
activity: Ask fingerpicking or strumming; teach one pattern; repeat four times
win_condition: Jen repeats one pattern four times without stopping
step_down_if_stuck: Use muted strings or open strings only

teaching_phrase: Neither is better. They are two colours.
activity: Four rest strokes then four free strokes on open string
win_condition: Jen hears or feels one difference
step_down_if_stuck: Use only open high E string

teaching_phrase: The low E and A strings are like highways for finding home notes.
activity: Find A and C on low E; find E and D on A string
step_down_if_stuck: Use only A at low E fret 5

teaching_phrase: Pentatonic means five notes. Treat them like five words that already sound good together.
activity: Play A minor pentatonic slowly; stop on A; make three-note phrase
step_down_if_stuck: Use only D string 5-7 and G string 5

teaching_phrase: The left hand chooses notes; the right hand gives them pulse.
activity: Review her riff or build one from three notes plus one right-hand rhythm
win_condition: Jen leaves with one repeatable riff

teaching_phrase: Conversation needs space. If you never pause, nobody can answer.
activity: Question phrase and answer phrase using pentatonic notes
win_condition: Jen plays one question and one answer
step_down_if_stuck: Use only rhythm on one note

teaching_phrase: We are just touching this gap, not mastering it today.
activity: Place C chord slowly and identify hard finger/string

teaching_phrase: What sounded most like music today?
activity: Log body/right-hand/fretboard/riff/fog; assign right-hand pattern E/A notes and riff
